header.title: Variables, Data Types & Operators
header.subtitle: Foundation Level • 45 minutes • Learn the fundamentals of Python data

introduction.title: Introduction to Python Fundamentals
introduction.paragraph1: Welcome to the foundation of Python programming! In this lesson, you'll learn how to store and manipulate data using variables, understand different data types, and perform operations with operators.
introduction.callout: What you'll learn: By the end of this lesson, you'll understand how to create variables, work with numbers and text, make logical decisions with booleans, and perform calculations and comparisons using operators.
introduction.whyParagraph: Variables and data types are the building blocks of every Python program. They allow you to:
whyList: Build complex applications from simple components

variables.title: Variables in Python
variables.paragraph1: Variables are like containers that store data values. In Python, you create a variable by simply assigning a value to a name using the equals sign (=).
variables.dynamicTypingParagraph: Python is dynamically typed, meaning you don't need to declare the type of a variable. The type is determined automatically based on the value you assign.

numbers.title: Working with Numbers
numbers.paragraph1: Python supports two main types of numbers: integers (whole numbers) and floats (decimal numbers). You can perform various mathematical operations with them.

strings.title: Working with Strings
strings.paragraph1: Strings are sequences of characters used to represent text. Python provides powerful tools for creating and manipulating strings.

booleans.title: Boolean Values
booleans.paragraph1: Booleans represent truth values: True or False. They're essential for making decisions in your programs.

operators.title: Python Operators
operators.paragraph1: Operators are special symbols that perform operations on variables and values. Python has several types of operators.

practice.title: Practice Exercises
practice.exercise1Description: Create variables to store your personal information and print a formatted introduction.
practice.exercise2Description: Create a simple calculator that performs basic operations on two numbers.
practice.exercise3Description: Work with string methods to clean and format text data.
practice.ctaDescription: Take our interactive quiz to see how well you've mastered variables, data types, and operators!
